summary: This component creates a 'TL;DR' (Too Long; Didn't Read) summary box for blog posts. It takes the summary content as children, extracts plain text from it to create structured data for search engines, and renders both the visible summary box and the metadata that search engines need to understand the post's abstract.

explanations.8: This function recursively walks through React node structures (which can be nested objects, arrays, or text) and extracts all the plain text from them, which is needed because search engines want plain text, not React components.
explanations.13: This line safely digs into a React node's props to find its children—it uses optional chaining (?.) so it won't crash if the node doesn't have a props object or if props doesn't have children.
explanations.25: useMemo caches the structured data object so it only gets recalculated when `children` changes, avoiding unnecessary work on every render.
explanations.37: This creates a JSON-LD script tag, which is a standard way to embed structured data that search engines can read to understand what the content is about.
explanations.42: role='region' tells screen readers this is an important section, and aria-label provides a label so users with screen readers understand what this box is for.
